sources.entry: ChartDB - Database diagrams editor that allows you to visualize and design your DB with a single query. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: ChartDB is an open-source, web-based database diagramming editor that visualizes and edits a database schema imported via a single query.
summary.what_it_does: Users run a provided "Smart Query" against their database, which returns the schema as JSON, and paste that JSON into ChartDB to get an interactive diagram. The editor allows adjusting the layout and adding annotations to the schema. It can generate DDL SQL scripts in a chosen dialect, which the README presents as a way to help migrate between databases such as MySQL to PostgreSQL. The README lists support for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MariaDB, SQLite (plus Cloudflare D1), CockroachDB, and ClickHouse. AI-assisted export requires an OpenAI API key or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint and model name.
use_cases: visualize an existing database schema as a diagram
design or annotate database tables and relationships
export DDL SQL scripts for a target dialect
migrate schema from one database engine to another
document database structure for team discussions
how_to_run: docker build -t chartdb . && docker run -e OPENAI_API_KEY= -p 8080:80 chartdb
notable: No account or database password needed; schema is imported through a single query returning JSON
AI-powered DDL export into the dialect of your choice
Supports seven SQL databases including ClickHouse and Cloudflare D1
Custom LLM inference endpoint support (e.g. local vLLM server)
Analytics can be turned off with DISABLE_ANALYTICS
caveats: README describes the project as in Public Beta
AI export features require an OpenAI API key or a custom endpoint; the two configuration options must not be mixed
Analytics via Fathom Analytics are enabled by default unless disabled
